note: Judgements from sources and our own adapter work on the date shown, not benchmarks. A tool marked not run was scored from its description only, and a source marked not fetched was not read.

groups.job: Where the company writes things down (wiki or notes tool)

recommendation.beginner: Keep writing where the team already writes. If there is no place yet, start with the plain folder template in this repo: it needs no account and Lorefern reads it directly.
recommendation.implementer: Notion has a read only adapter here that was tested against a local stand in, not against Notion. For Docmost, Outline, Wiki.js or BookStack, export to Markdown into the company folder and let Lorefern read the folder. That path is tested.
recommendation.cost_sensitive: A Markdown folder in Git costs nothing. Docmost, Outline, Wiki.js and BookStack are open source and cost a small server. Notion has its own price page; read it yourself.
recommendation.open_source_when: Open source wikis are the right call when the client wants documents on their own server or the team can run Docker. They are the wrong call when the team already lives in Notion and will not move.

groups.job: Search index for the knowledge base

recommendation.beginner: Keep the built in SQLite search for a demo and for a small company. You do not need to set up anything else.
recommendation.implementer: Use SQLite full text for a single client on one server, Postgres full text when the client runs on Postgres. Add real embeddings only after you measure that keyword search misses too many questions (the held out numbers in this repo show it does for wording that differs from the pages).
recommendation.cost_sensitive: Both full text options cost nothing extra. A hosted vector database adds a monthly bill and a second place your data lives.
recommendation.open_source_when: Open source search is the right call for a company knowledge base of a few thousand pages. A hosted vector database is worth it when meaning based search over a large, changing set matters more than cost.
